chapter: New York arrival, Billy Hicks and the Black Cat
title: The white beginnings of 52nd Street and Teddy Wilson's Famous Door date
summary: Hall says Black musicians worked above 110th Street, and recalls the Teddy Wilson band opening at the Famous Door in 1939.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When they found out they could get a draw. Those were hard times, there was -- we weren't working below 110th Street at this period of time. It wasn't until '39, '37 that the Spirits of Rhythm were working at the Street and Louis Prima was working at Jimmy Ryan's and Eddie Condon was working at Gallaher's and this was strictly a white --
Right, the beginning of 52nd Street was a white thing.

Right. So with Teddy Wilson's big band, we opened at the Famous Door in May '39 and the band was too cool for what they expected and we started out with a notice, that they wanted to get rid of us right away.

Yeah, then after a week or so they realized that we were a pretty good band, but they had already booked Charlie Barnet to follow us, so that would be the end of our 52nd Street career. But then by the same token, John Kirby
just opened at the Onxy Club; Stuff Smith -- Stuff Smith had opened the Onyx Club --
This is prewar, World War Two.
But up until then you were up above 110th Street.
No, other than the Arcadia Ballroom, where Fletcher and Roy had a big band.
